summary: Hudson-Athens Lighthouse in the Hudson River: an 1874 caisson light automated in 1949, now owned by HALPS, endangered by foundation damage and a 2025 barge strike.

notes_for_editor: Conflicts left open, flagged in the story where they matter: first lens order (sixth per LF, fifth per USLHS); focal plane 46 ft (LF) vs 52 ft above MHW (USLHS record; the record's 14.0 m follows LF); pilings: LF (pilings driven 50 ft, limestone pier) vs Times Union (200 wood pilings driven 50 ft); Frank Best's service: archive 1893-1918 vs LF 'after his death in 1892'; Nellie Best listed as principal keeper for 1918 by the archive vs LF's account that she resigned; LF says Brunner was the last civilian keeper, but the archive lists three more keepers to 1986 with no role given in the sources read; title: LF says the title passed to HALPS on 3 July 2000, while the Times Union (2023) describes HALPS as a lessee since 1984 and NTHP calls HALPS the 'owners'; check the county deed before publishing 'owned by'. 2022 state grant: LF says the state parks agency granted $500,000 in January 2022 to replace the roof; Times Union says the society has begun repairs with it, which only stabilises the structure. The story now states both. Characteristic: the record's 'Fl G 2.5s' conflicts with the Wikidata value 'Oc G 2.5s' (both lead-only). LF's 1926 description is a white flash every two seconds; its current characteristic is not confirmed by a readable source, so none is given in facts. LF says the city of Hudson was 'chartered on the west bank of the river'; the story omits the bank. Secondary sources only for: the Bertha Munn memoir (LF quoting a 1960 Chatham Courier article); Murray's account (LF, origin not stated); the 1935 peach-jar accident (LF, citing a New York Post article not read); the 1946 Saturday Evening Post cover (LF; not read). Newspaper searches (Chronicling America: 1874 'Middle Ground' lighthouse; 1912 Isabella collision; 1918 Nellie Best) found no readable hit about this station; none used. A 2026 Times Union/Yahoo report on the Coast Guard closing its barge-strike probe at a $50,000 estimate was seen only in search snippets and is not used. HALPS homepage news items are undated; no tour dates were used. The NRHP nomination PDF (npgallery 79003796) is a 'not yet digitized' placeholder. Wikipedia was read for leads only and is not cited. Stations' Little Gull Island record (us-ny-little-gull-island) carries Murray 1909-1918 as head keeper; other_stations entry added with LF as the connecting source. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-22: The story now states the disagreements it had left out: the fog bell date (LF 15 July 1894; the 1895 report gives 15 and 16 July in different places, scan pages 29 and 87); Frank Best's start (LF after his father's 1892 death; archive 1893); the 2022 grant (see above). The Brunner eye injury is now quoted as LighthouseFriends prints it (her eye had to be removed; the glass went into the left eye). The 1946 cover is credited to the artist, Mead Schaeffer, who had the family pose. The 'Date Published' in the NRHP asset record (5/29/1979) is now given as the record date. The 1899 page (scan 110) and the 1895 fog-bell pages (scan 29, 87) were confirmed with corpus.py page. The HALPS homepage is used for the restoration-focus sentence; its news items are undated. COPYRIGHT PASS 2026-10-22: Quotations from copyrighted sources (LighthouseFriends, the museum site, the Times Union, the National Trust, HALPS) were reworded in the story; the remaining quoted text is the Light-House Board, Commissioner and keeper-log wording (public domain), one museum title, and short names. The evidence quotes in this file are internal and were left exact.
